hasHsa.ask: Contributions to a health savings account (HSA)
hasHsa.help: Money you put into an HSA yourself for 2025, not through your employer's payroll (that is in box 12 of your W-2, code W, and isn't deducted again). You need a high-deductible health plan (Form 8889).

hsaContributions.ask: HSA contributions you made yourself for 2025
hsaContributions.help: Including what you add by April 15, 2026 for 2025. Your HSA's Form 5498-SA shows them.

optionLabels.family: You and at least one other person (family coverage)

hsaAllYear.ask: Did the plan cover you in every month of 2025?

optionLabels.no: No, only part of the year

hsaNonMedical.ask: Did you take money out of the HSA for anything other than medical expenses?
hsaNonMedical.help: A Form 1099-SA shows distributions. Ones not for qualified medical expenses are taxed, with 20% more, on Form 8889.

hasIraContribution.help: Money you put into a traditional IRA for 2025, by April 15, 2026 (Schedule 1, line 20). Not a Roth IRA, and not a rollover.

iraContribution.help: Your IRA's Form 5498 shows them, or your statements if you contributed in 2026.

coveredByPlan.ask: An employer's retirement plan covered you in 2025
coveredByPlan.help: The "Retirement plan" box in box 13 of your W-2 is checked (a 401(k), 403(b), pension or the like). It can make your IRA deduction smaller.

livedInCaliforniaAllYear.ask: You lived in California all of 2025
livedInCaliforniaAllYear.help: California was your home (your domicile) for the whole year. If you moved in or out during 2025, or lived in another state for part of it, you file Form 540NR, which this app doesn't prepare.

caFullYearCoverage.ask: Everyone on your return had health coverage all of 2025
caFullYearCoverage.help: You, your spouse filing jointly, and anyone you claim had health insurance that counts as minimum essential coverage (from an employer, Covered California, Medi-Cal or Medicare Part A or C) in every month. Without it, California may charge a penalty (Form 540, line 92, and form FTB 3853), which this app doesn't work out.

caBondInterest.help: Of your tax-exempt interest (box 8 of your 1099-INT and box 12 of your 1099-DIV), the part from bonds of California, its cities and counties, or from a fund with at least half its assets in them (the fund's year-end statement says how much). California taxes the rest (Schedule CA, line 2, column C).

hsaEarnings.help: Interest, dividends and gains in your health savings account for 2025 (your HSA's statement shows them). California doesn't treat an HSA as tax-free, so they are taxed, and the HSA deduction and your employer's contributions are added back (Schedule CA, lines 1h, 2 and 13).

caCareInCalifornia.ask: All the care you paid for was given in California
caCareInCalifornia.help: The California credit for child and dependent care counts only care given in California (form FTB 3506).

caPaidRent.ask: You rented your home in California for at least half of 2025
caPaidRent.help: You paid rent for at least six months of 2025 on your main home in California. You don't qualify if it was exempt from property tax (such as a dormitory or military barracks), if you or your spouse got the homeowner's property tax exemption, or if you lived for more than half the year with someone who can claim you as a dependent (Nonrefundable Renter's Credit Qualification Record).

caEstimatedPayments.help: California estimated tax you paid for 2025 (Form 540-ES), any 2024 California refund you applied to 2025, and a payment with an extension (Form 540, line 72).

caUseTax.help: Use tax on things you bought from sellers outside California for use in California, without California sales tax (often online). Enter 0 if you owe none or paid it to the CDTFA. The Booklet's Use Tax Worksheet and table help you work it out (Form 540, line 91, which can't be left blank).

fosterYouth.ask: You were in California foster care at age 13 or older
fosterYouth.help: Placed through the California foster care system while 13 or older. From 18 to 25 you may get the Foster Youth Tax Credit (FTB 3514, Part IX).

paidForCare.ask: You paid for the care of a child under 13, or of a dependant who can't care for themselves, so you could work
paidForCare.help: Day care, a babysitter, before- or after-school care or a day camp in 2025, so you (and your spouse, filing jointly) could work or look for work. Not overnight camp, school from kindergarten up, or care by your spouse, the child's parent, your dependant or your child under 19 (Form 2441).

householdEmployer.ask: You paid a household employee, such as a nanny, $2,800 or more in 2025, or $1,000 or more in a calendar quarter of 2024 or 2025
householdEmployer.help: Someone who works in your home and does the work the way you tell them. You may owe household employment taxes on Schedule H.

priorYearCare.ask: You paid in 2025 for care given in 2024
priorYearCare.help: Care given in 2024 and paid for in 2025 can add to the 2025 credit (Form 2441, line 9b).

studentOrDisabledMonths.ask: Months of 2025 you were a full-time student or weren't able to care for yourself
studentOrDisabledMonths.help: Filing jointly, for each such month you are treated as earning at least $250 ($500 with two or more people in care), so the credit for child care can apply when one of you didn't work. Enter 0 if neither applies.

spouseNeedsCare.ask: Your spouse wasn't able to care for themselves, and you paid for their care
spouseNeedsCare.help: A spouse who can't dress, clean or feed themselves, or needs constant attention, and lived with you more than half of 2025.

cantCareForSelf.ask: Not able to care for themselves
cantCareForSelf.help: They can't dress, clean or feed themselves because of a physical or mental condition, or need constant attention to stay safe.

careExpenses.ask: Care you paid for them in 2025 so you could work
careExpenses.help: Paid in 2025 for care given in 2025, including what dependent care benefits from your employer paid. For a child who turned 13 in 2025, only care before their birthday. Not food, clothing, school from kindergarten up, or overnight camp.

careBenefitsCarriedOver.ask: Dependent care benefits from 2024 used in 2025's grace period
careBenefitsCarriedOver.help: Money left in a dependent care account at the end of 2024 that your employer let you use in early 2025 (Form 2441, line 13).

careBenefitsForfeited.ask: Dependent care benefits you lost or carried forward to 2026
careBenefitsForfeited.help: Money in a dependent care account for 2025 that you didn't use, because you had no care expenses for it (Form 2441, line 14).

optionLabels.child: Son, daughter, stepchild or adopted child
optionLabels.sibling: Brother, sister, half or step sibling
optionLabels.none: Not related, lived with you all year

monthsWithYou.ask: Months they lived with you in 2025
monthsWithYou.help: Count time away at school, in hospital or on vacation as time with you. For a child born or who died in 2025, count the months they were alive.

fullTimeStudent.ask: A full-time student in at least 5 months of 2025

paidOwnSupport.ask: Paid over half of their own support in 2025

filedJointReturn.help: Answer no if they file jointly only to get back tax withheld.

citizenOrResident.ask: A U.S. citizen, U.S. national or U.S. resident alien

grossIncome.help: Income that isn't exempt from tax, such as wages and interest; not social security benefits.

supportedByYou.ask: You paid over half of their support in 2025

hasSSN.ask: Has a social security number valid for employment
hasSSN.help: Issued by the due date of the return. The child tax credit needs one; without it, the credit for other dependents may apply.

claimedBy.help: Filing separately, each dependant is claimed on one spouse's return.

hasValidSSN.ask: You have a social security number valid for employment
hasValidSSN.help: Issued by the due date of the return. The child tax credit needs one (filing jointly, one spouse's is enough); the earned income credit needs one for you and, filing jointly, for your spouse; the deductions for tips and overtime need one for the person who received them.

paidHalfOfHome.ask: You paid over half the cost of keeping up your home in 2025
paidHalfOfHome.help: Rent or mortgage interest, property tax, utilities, repairs and food eaten at home. Head of household and qualifying surviving spouse need it, and so does the credit for child care when filing separately.

spouseDiedIn2023Or2024.help: With a dependent child who lived with you all year, you may file as a qualifying surviving spouse.

paidForEducation.ask: You paid for college or other higher education in 2025, for yourself or for a dependant
paidForEducation.help: Tuition and required fees for a university, college, vocational school or other school after high school that can take part in federal student aid. A Form 1098-T from the school shows what it received. It can give you the American opportunity credit or the lifetime learning credit (Form 8863). Each dependant's expenses are asked under their name.

educationExpenses.ask: Your own qualified education expenses in 2025
educationExpenses.help: Tuition and the fees and course materials the school requires, that you paid in 2025 for your own courses, less tax-free scholarships, grants and employer education aid. Start from box 1 of your Form 1098-T, less box 5. Not room and board, insurance, medical expenses or transportation. Enter 0 if you weren't a student.

educationCredit.help: The American opportunity credit is larger and partly refundable, but all of these must be true: the courses lead to a degree or other recognized credential; the student was enrolled at least half-time for at least one academic period that began in 2025; the student hadn't completed the first 4 years of college before 2025; the credit wasn't claimed for the student for 4 earlier years; and the student has no felony drug conviction. Otherwise, the lifetime learning credit counts any course at an eligible school, even one to improve job skills.

optionLabels.aotc: American opportunity credit (all of its conditions are true)

parentAlive.ask: At least one of your parents was alive at the end of 2025
parentAlive.help: With the American opportunity credit, someone under 24 who isn't filing jointly may get no refundable part of it (Form 8863, line 7).

fullTimeStudentSelf.ask: You were a full-time student in at least 5 months of 2025

earnedUnderHalfSupport.ask: Your earned income was less than half of your support in 2025
earnedUnderHalfSupport.help: Earned income is wages and self-employment income. Support is food, housing, clothing, medical care, education and the like, paid by you, your parents and others. A scholarship isn't support if you were a full-time student.

studentExpenses.ask: Qualified education expenses you paid for them in 2025
studentExpenses.help: Tuition and the fees and course materials the school requires, paid in 2025 by you or by them, less tax-free scholarships, grants and employer education aid. Start from box 1 of their Form 1098-T, less box 5. Not room and board. Enter 0 if they weren't a student after high school.

studentCredit.help: The American opportunity credit is larger and partly refundable, but all of these must be true: the courses lead to a degree or other recognized credential; the student was enrolled at least half-time for at least one academic period that began in 2025; the student hadn't completed the first 4 years of college before 2025; the credit wasn't claimed for the student for 4 earlier years; and the student has no felony drug conviction. Otherwise, the lifetime learning credit counts any course at an eligible school, even one to improve job skills.

optionLabels.aotc: American opportunity credit (all of its conditions are true)

hasStudentLoan.help: Interest you paid in 2025 on a loan taken out only to pay higher education expenses for you, your spouse or your dependant (Schedule 1, line 21). Your lender's Form 1098-E shows it. Filing separately, or if someone can claim you as a dependent, you can't deduct it.

studentLoanInterest.ask: Student loan interest not on a Form 1098-E
studentLoanInterest.help: Uploaded Forms 1098-E are added. Enter interest you paid in 2025 that isn't on one (a lender sends it only for $600 or more): the interest only, not the payments of the loan itself.

livedApartLastSixMonths.ask: You and your spouse lived apart for the last 6 months of 2025
livedApartLastSixMonths.help: Filing separately, you can get the earned income credit (with a qualifying child) or the credit for child care only if you didn't share a home with your spouse for the last 6 months of 2025.

hasDividends.help: A Form 1099-DIV from each fund, broker or company that paid you $10 or more of dividends or capital gain distributions.

hasBrokerSales.ask: Sales of stocks, bonds or funds
hasBrokerSales.help: A Form 1099-B from each broker. A broker's yearly statement usually sums the sales up by part of Form 8949 (box A, B, D or E): enter one 1099-B for each part, with its proceeds and cost.

hasLossCarryover.ask: A capital loss carried over from 2024
hasLossCarryover.help: A capital loss larger than the $3,000 ($1,500 filing separately) you could deduct in an earlier year carries over. Your 2024 Schedule D, or its Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet, shows it.

shortLossCarryover.help: Schedule D, line 6. Enter it as a positive amount.

longLossCarryover.help: Schedule D, line 14. Enter it as a positive amount.

hasItemized.help: Mortgage interest on your home, state and local taxes (income or property), gifts to charity and medical expenses (Schedule A). The app takes them instead of the standard deduction when they are larger. Your W-2s' state income tax (box 17) is counted for you.

itemMedical.help: What you paid in 2025 for medical and dental care, prescriptions and health insurance premiums for you and your family, less what insurance or anyone else paid back. Only the part over 7.5% of your AGI counts.

itemStateTax.ask: State and local income tax paid in 2025, not on a W-2
itemStateTax.help: Estimated state tax payments for 2025, and a balance you paid in 2025 for 2024. Box 17 of your W-2s is already counted.

itemRealEstateTax.help: Property tax you paid in 2025 on your home or land, yourself or through your lender (box 10 of a Form 1098 often shows it).

itemPersonalPropertyTax.help: A yearly tax based on the value of a car or boat, for example.

itemMortgageOther.ask: Mortgage interest not on a Form 1098
itemMortgageOther.help: Uploaded Forms 1098 are counted. Enter 0 unless you paid interest to a person rather than a lender.

mortgageQualifies.help: Each loan was taken out to buy, build or improve the home it is secured by (your main home or a second home), and all of them together are $750,000 or less ($375,000 filing separately; $1,000,000 for loans before December 16, 2017).

optionLabels.yes: Yes, both of these are true

itemCashGifts.ask: Gifts to charity by cash, check or card
itemCashGifts.help: To churches, schools, charities and other qualified organizations, with a receipt or bank record for each.

itemNoncashGifts.ask: Gifts to charity of things, not money
itemNoncashGifts.help: The fair market value of clothes, furniture or other things you gave. Over $500 in all needs Form 8283.

livedInNewYorkAllYear.ask: You lived in New York State all of 2025
livedInNewYorkAllYear.help: New York was your home (your domicile) for the whole year. If you moved in or out during 2025, you file Form IT-203 as a part-year resident, which this app doesn't prepare.

nyLocality.ask: Where you lived in New York in 2025
nyLocality.help: New York City and Yonkers have their own income tax on the New York return. Someone who moved in or out of either during 2025 files Form IT-360.1, which this app doesn't prepare.

optionLabels.elsewhere: Outside New York City and Yonkers, all year
optionLabels.nyc: New York City (the Bronx, Brooklyn, Manhattan, Queens or Staten Island), all year
optionLabels.partYear: New York City or Yonkers for only part of the year

nyBondInterest.ask: Tax-exempt interest from New York bonds
nyBondInterest.help: Of your tax-exempt interest (box 8 of your 1099-INT and box 12 of your 1099-DIV), the part from bonds of New York State or its local governments, or from a fund's New York bonds (the fund's year-end statement says how much). New York taxes the rest (Form IT-201, line 20).

nyPublicRetirement.help: Only for an employee of New York State or a local government in New York: the 414(h) retirement contributions in box 14 of your W-2 (with the New York City flexible benefits program, IRC 125, if you work for New York City). New York adds them back (Form IT-201, line 21). Enter 0 if you have none.

nyOtherAdditions.ask: You have another New York addition
nyOtherAdditions.help: Such as a withdrawal from a New York 529 college savings account not used for education, or another addition of Form IT-225. This app doesn't work them out (Form IT-201, lines 22 and 23).

nyGovernmentPension.ask: Your pension from New York State, a New York local government or the federal government
nyGovernmentPension.help: Of your taxable pensions, annuities and IRA distributions, the part paid by a pension plan of New York State, its local governments, certain public authorities or the U.S. government (including the military). New York doesn't tax it (Form IT-201, line 26). Enter 0 if none of it is.

nyPensionAfter59.ask: Your taxable pension and IRA income received after you turned 59½
nyPensionAfter59.help: You turned 59½ during 2025, so New York excludes only the pension, annuity and IRA income paid to you after that day, up to $20,000 (Form IT-201, line 29). Leave out a pension from New York State, a local government or the federal government.

nyOtherSubtractions.ask: You have another New York subtraction
nyOtherSubtractions.help: Such as a refund of state or local income tax you included in income, or another subtraction of Form IT-225. This app doesn't work them out (Form IT-201, lines 25 and 31).

ny529.ask: Contributions to a New York 529 college savings account you own
ny529.help: What you put in 2025 into a New York's 529 College Savings Program account you are the owner of. New York subtracts up to $5,000 for each owner (Form IT-201, line 30). Enter 0 if none.

nyBusinessZone.ask: Where your business is carried on
nyBusinessZone.help: Net earnings from self-employment of more than $50,000 in New York City or the seven counties near it have the metropolitan commuter transportation mobility tax (MCTMT, Form IT-201, lines 54a to 54e). Splitting earnings between places needs Form IT-203-A, which this app doesn't prepare.

optionLabels.zone2: All in Dutchess, Nassau, Orange, Putnam, Rockland, Suffolk or Westchester County (Zone 2)
optionLabels.both: Partly in those counties and partly outside, or in both zones

nyUnder4CareExpenses.ask: Care expenses you paid for children under 4
nyUnder4CareExpenses.help: Of your care expenses, the part for children who were under 4 at the end of 2025. The New York City child care credit counts only that part (Form IT-216, line 23).

nyTuition.ask: Undergraduate tuition you paid for your own courses in 2025
nyTuition.help: Tuition only (not fees, books, room or board) for undergraduate courses at a college or university, less scholarships and grants that paid it. It gives the New York college tuition credit (Form IT-272). Enter 0 for graduate courses.

nyStudentTuition.ask: Undergraduate tuition you paid for them in 2025
nyStudentTuition.help: Tuition only (not fees, books, room or board) for their undergraduate courses at a college or university, less scholarships and grants that paid it. It gives the New York college tuition credit (Form IT-272). Enter 0 for graduate courses.

nyRealPropertyCredit.ask: You rented or owned your home in New York and lived there at least six months of 2025
nyRealPropertyCredit.help: With a household income of $18,000 or less, you may get the real property tax credit (Form IT-214), which this app doesn't prepare.

nyEstimatedPayments.help: New York State, New York City and Yonkers estimated tax you paid for 2025 (Form IT-2105), any 2024 New York refund you applied to 2025, and a payment with an extension (Form IT-370) (Form IT-201, line 75).

nySalesTax.ask: New York sales or use tax
nySalesTax.help: Sales or use tax on things you bought for use in New York without paying New York sales tax (often online or out of state). Enter 0 if you owe none. The Instructions' Sales and use tax worksheet and chart help you work it out (Form IT-201, line 59, which can't be left blank).

canBeClaimed.ask: Someone can claim you as a dependent
canBeClaimed.help: A parent or other person can claim you as a dependent on their 2025 return, even if they don't. Your standard deduction is then smaller (Form 1040, line 12a).

isBlind.help: Totally or partly blind on December 31, 2025, as a doctor certifies (Form 1040, line 12d). It adds to your standard deduction.

spouseItemizes.ask: Your spouse itemizes deductions on their separate return
spouseItemizes.help: When a married couple files separately and one of them itemizes on Schedule A, the other must itemize too (Form 1040, line 12b).

spouseDiedIn2025.help: A spouse who died during 2025 lets you file a joint return for 2025.

hasWages.help: A Form W-2 from each employer you worked for in 2025.

hasInterest.help: A Form 1099-INT from each bank, credit union or broker that paid you $10 or more of interest, and from the Treasury for savings bonds.

hasTipsOrOvertime.help: Tips you received in a tipped job, or overtime pay for hours over 40 a week. For 2025 you can deduct qualified tips and the "half" of time-and-a-half overtime on Schedule 1-A; filing separately, you can't.

hasOtherIncome.help: Income not asked above, such as unemployment compensation (Form 1099-G), a state tax refund that is taxable, rent or royalties (Schedule E), alimony, gambling winnings (Form W-2G), prizes, jury duty pay, a canceled debt, or income from a partnership, S corporation, estate or trust (Schedule K-1). This app doesn't take it yet: the return says so instead of leaving it out.

estimatedPayments.help: Estimated tax you paid for 2025, and any 2024 refund you applied to 2025 (Form 1040, line 26).

hasIraDistribution.help: A Form 1099-R from each IRA you took money out of, rolled over or converted, with the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box checked.

hasPension.ask: Pensions, annuities or retirement plan distributions
hasPension.help: A Form 1099-R from each pension, annuity, 401(k), 403(b) or other plan that paid you, with the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box not checked.

hasSocialSecurity.help: The Form SSA-1099 the Social Security Administration sends each January.

iraBasis.ask: You made nondeductible contributions to a traditional IRA (Form 8606)
iraBasis.help: Contributions you made in any year without deducting them are your basis: part of each distribution is then tax free, figured on Form 8606. Your earlier Forms 8606 show it. Most people answer No.

indirectRollover.ask: You put money from a distribution back into an IRA or plan yourself, within 60 days
indirectRollover.help: A rollover the payer didn't make for you (box 7 isn't G or H). The amount you put back isn't taxed, which this app doesn't work out yet.

earlyException.ask: An exception to the 10% additional tax applies to a distribution with code 1
earlyException.help: Code 1 in box 7 means you were under 59½. You owe 10% more on the taxable amount, unless an exception applies (such as disability, medical expenses over 7.5% of AGI, a first home up to $10,000 from an IRA, higher education from an IRA, or a separation from service in or after the year you turned 55). An exception is claimed on Form 5329, which this app doesn't prepare.

livedApartAllYear.ask: You and your spouse lived apart all of 2025
livedApartAllYear.help: Filing separately, more of your social security benefits are taxable if you lived with your spouse at any time in 2025 (Form 1040, line 6d).

qualifiedTips.help: Tips customers chose to give you, in cash or by card, in a job on the IRS's list of tipped occupations (such as wait staff, bartenders, hairdressers, delivery and rideshare drivers; see IRS.gov/TippedOccupations). Box 7 of your W-2 shows the tips you reported to your employer, and is the amount to start from. Not service charges or automatic gratuities. Enter 0 if your job isn't on the list.

qualifiedOvertime.help: Only the "half" of time-and-a-half that the Fair Labor Standards Act requires for hours over 40 a week, in a job that is not exempt from overtime. Your employer may show it in box 14 of your W-2 or on a statement. If you only know the total paid for your overtime hours at time-and-a-half, divide it by 3. Not pay above time-and-a-half, holiday or weekend premiums, or overtime paid under state rules only.

hasCarLoan.ask: Interest on a loan for a new car
hasCarLoan.help: Interest you paid in 2025 on a loan you took out after 2024 to buy a new car, minivan, van, SUV, pickup truck or motorcycle (Schedule 1-A, Part IV). A lease doesn't count.

carLoanInterest.ask: Interest you paid on the loan in 2025
carLoanInterest.help: The interest only, not the payments of the loan itself. Your lender's statement shows it.

carLoanQualifies.help: All of these are true: the car was new when you bought it (its first use started with you); its final assembly was in the United States (the label on the car, or the plant in its VIN, says so); you expect to use it for personal use more than half the time; and the loan is in your name and secured by a first lien on the car. You write the car's VIN on Schedule 1-A yourself.

optionLabels.yes: Yes, all of these are true

hasSelfEmployment.help: Income from your own business as a sole proprietor: freelancing, contract or gig work, a shop or a trade (Schedule C). A Form 1099-NEC, 1099-K or 1099-MISC often shows it. One business for each person.

businessIncome.help: Each Form 1099-NEC you add is counted. Enter everything else the business was paid in 2025: cash, cards, payment apps and platforms (a Form 1099-K), checks. Leave out sales tax you collected.

businessCar.help: The business part only: the standard mileage rate (70 cents a mile for 2025) times your business miles, or the business share of your actual costs, plus parking and tolls.

businessContractLabor.help: What you paid people who aren't your employees.

businessOffice.help: Postage, software subscriptions, stationery and other office costs.

businessRent.help: Rent for an office, a shop or a stall. Not for your home.

businessTravel.help: Business trips away from home overnight. Not meals, which are asked next.

businessMeals.help: The full cost; half of it is deducted.

businessUtilities.help: For business property, and the business part of your phone and internet.

businessOtherExpenses.help: Fees, bank charges, education for the business and other costs not above. List them in Part V of Schedule C.

businessExtras.ask: Anything else on your Schedule C

optionLabels.assets: Equipment, a vehicle or other property to depreciate (Form 4562)
optionLabels.inventory: Goods you make or buy to sell (cost of goods sold)

F1098T.about: From a college, university or other eligible school: the tuition and required fees it was paid for the student in 2025, and the scholarships or grants it handled

boxes.1: Payments received for qualified tuition and related expenses
boxes.4: Adjustments made for a prior year
boxes.6: Adjustments to scholarships or grants for a prior year

F1098E.about: From a lender, the interest it received in 2025 on a student loan

boxes.1: Student loan interest received by lender

F1098E.name: 1098-E

DIV.about: Dividends and capital gain distributions a fund, broker or company paid you, and any federal income tax withheld

boxes.13: Specified private activity bond interest dividends

DIV.name: 1099-DIV

B.title: Form 1099-B Proceeds From Broker Transactions
B.about: What a broker reports of sales of stocks, bonds, funds or other securities. Enter one summary for each part of Form 8949 the broker's statement names (box A, B, D or E)

boxes.CAT: The part of Form 8949 (A, B, D or E)

B.name: 1099-B

F1098.title: Form 1098 Mortgage Interest Statement
F1098.about: From a lender, the interest and points you paid in 2025 on a mortgage on your home

RIRA.about: A distribution from a traditional, Roth, SEP or SIMPLE IRA, with the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box checked

R.title: Form 1099-R Distributions From Pensions, Annuities, Retirement Plans
R.about: A pension, an annuity, or a distribution from a 401(k), 403(b) or other retirement plan, with the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box not checked

boxes.5: Employee contributions/Designated Roth contributions or insurance premiums

R.name: 1099-R

SSA.title: Form SSA-1099 Social Security Benefit Statement
SSA.about: The social security benefits paid to you in 2025, and any federal income tax withheld from them
SSA.name: SSA-1099

NEC.title: Form 1099-NEC Nonemployee Compensation
NEC.about: What a business paid you for work as a contractor or freelancer, not as its employee, and any federal income tax it withheld
NEC.name: 1099-NEC

W2.title: Form W-2 Wage and Tax Statement
W2.about: Wages an employer paid, and the federal income, social security and Medicare tax it withheld

boxes.12W: Box 12, code W: employer contributions to your health savings account

W2.name: W-2

INT.about: Interest a bank, credit union, broker or the U.S. Treasury paid, and any federal income tax withheld

boxes.3: Interest on U.S. Savings Bonds and Treasury obligations

INT.name: 1099-INT

fileJointly.title: Filing jointly would cost you less
fileJointly.text: You and your spouse file separately. Filed jointly, as one return with both your incomes, the two of you would pay less, as worked out from what you entered. Filing separately keeps each of you liable only for your own return, but it gives up the earned income credit, the education credits, the student loan interest deduction and the tips and overtime deductions, and most of the child care credit. To file jointly, choose it on Personal info.

fileSeparately.title: Filing separately would cost you less

estimatedTaxPenalty.title: You may owe a penalty for paying too little during the year
estimatedTaxPenalty.text: You owe $1,000 or more, and more than a tenth of the tax shown on your return (line 24, less the refundable credits on lines 27a to 29). The IRS may then charge a penalty for not paying enough tax during the year, through withholding or estimated payments, unless an exception applies (for example, you paid at least your 2024 tax). This app doesn't work out the penalty (Form 2210): leave line 38 blank, and the IRS works it out and sends you a bill. To avoid it next year, have more withheld on Form W-4.

reading.documents: United States information returns (Forms W-2, 1099, 1098 and SSA-1099)
notes: Box numbers with a letter are written in capitals: box 1a of a 1099-DIV is 1A, box 2a of a 1099-R is 2A, box 1d of a 1099-B is 1D.

A W-2 prints boxes 1 to 20. Box 12 holds codes with amounts: report only the amount with code W, under 12W. Boxes 13 and 14 aren't read. The 'a' to 'f' boxes hold numbers, names and addresses, never amounts: leave them out. Box 15 holds a state's two-letter code and the employer's state ID number: report only the code (CA), under 15, with that state's wages (16) and income tax (17). Boxes 18 to 20 are a locality's wages, income tax and name: report them when box 20 names New York City (NYC, NY CITY, NEW YORK CITY: report NYC) or Yonkers (report YONKERS); for any other locality report 18 and 19 and leave 20 out. A W-2 with two states or two localities has a second line of boxes 15 to 20: return it as two W-2s, one per line, the federal boxes on the first.

On a 1099, the state boxes give the state's two-letter code (under 15 on a 1099-INT and a 1099-R, 14 on a 1099-DIV, 6 on a 1099-NEC; the payer's state number after it isn't read) and the state tax withheld (17 on a 1099-INT, 16 on a 1099-DIV, 14 on a 1099-R, 5 on a 1099-NEC). A 1099-R's boxes 16 to 19 are the state distribution, the local tax withheld, the locality's name (NYC for New York City, YONKERS for Yonkers; leave 18 out for any other place) and the local distribution. Leave them out when they are blank.

On a 1099 or 1098, report the payer's, lender's or school's name as issuer. A form can print a box that is a checkbox (such as boxes 7, 8 and 9 of a 1098-T): leave checkboxes out, unless the list names one.

A Form 1099-R is type RIRA when its IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box is checked, and type R when it isn't. Its box 7 holds one or two distribution codes: report the first under 7 and a second, if any, under 7B (box 7 of 7D is 7, and D under 7B).

A broker's Form 1099-B usually comes as a yearly statement that sums the sales up by part of Form 8949: 'Box A' (short-term, basis reported to the IRS), 'Box B' (short-term, not reported), 'Box D' (long-term, reported), 'Box E' (long-term, not reported). Return one 1099-B for each part that has sales, with that letter under CAT and the part's totals: proceeds (1D), cost or other basis (1E), accrued market discount (1F) and wash sale loss disallowed (1G). Federal income tax withheld (box 4) goes on the first.
A broker's statement often holds a 1099-DIV and a 1099-INT too: return them as well.

For a Form 1098-T, person is the student, and issuer the school. For a Form 1098-E, person is the borrower, and issuer the lender. For a Form 1098, person is the borrower, and issuer the lender. For a Form SSA-1099, person is the beneficiary, and issuer is Social Security Administration.
A corrected form (marked CORRECTED) replaces the first one: read it like any other.
